ICMP ping state machine for peers, with add/remove, timeout, and reply handling.

# Purpose
`fd_ssping.c` implements a peer ping manager for IPv4 endpoints. It keeps a pool of peer records, a hash map from `fd_ip4_port_t` to peer state, and five deadline lists that track peers in the `UNPINGED`, `PINGED`, `VALID`, `REFRESHING`, and `INVALID` states. The code creates and manages an ICMP datagram socket, sends ICMP echo requests in bursts with `sendmmsg`, receives echo replies with `recvfrom`, and measures round-trip latency for each peer. It also stores a UDP port in each ping packet so the reply can be matched to the correct peer entry, since ICMP does not carry a UDP port field.

The file exposes the main lifecycle and control functions for the ping subsystem: [`fd_ssping_new`](<#fd_ssping_new>), [`fd_ssping_join`](<#fd_ssping_join>), [`fd_ssping_get_sockfd`](<#fd_ssping_get_sockfd>), [`fd_ssping_add`](<#fd_ssping_add>), [`fd_ssping_remove`](<#fd_ssping_remove>), [`fd_ssping_invalidate`](<#fd_ssping_invalidate>), and [`fd_ssping_advance`](<#fd_ssping_advance>). [`fd_ssping_advance`](<#fd_ssping_advance>) drives the state machine by sending new pings, moving peers between deadline lists, expiring peers that do not reply in time, and notifying `fd_sspeer_selector_remove` when a peer becomes invalid. The file also uses an `on_ping` callback to report successful replies and measured latency to the caller.
